9648335761625202777: "Merchants may obsess over profit, but rules are required regardless to maintain balance." — Unknown Priest of Talanton Balance Coins, the smallest unit of trade decreed by Talanton, as well as their gift to humanity. In the present world, Balance Coins take the form of tiny gravel-like weights that can be mixed into bigger weights with any amount like clay. It is because of this that a single Balance Coin simply can't be carried, and trade between city-states requires dromas transportation to move obscene weights of currency. But no one can deny that this linear calculation method is indeed very "fair." The history of Balance Coins can be traced back to the ancient Era Chrysea's nascent period. Before that, city-states bartered using objects of Titan worship, such as shells, feathers, redsoil clay blocks, etc. As the city-states' supplies became more abundant, along with increasing demand for inter-city trade, merchants urgently needed some common equivalent as a medium of exchange. Gold, silver, and other precious metals came into the picture — rare in production quantity, stable in value, and effective in reducing friction during trade. From that point on, trade among the various city-states gradually gravitated towards precious metals. But even the face value of the lightest copper coin far exceeded the cost of one stalk of vegetable, and this brought much inconvenience to the commonfolk. During the economic development of the various city-states, many precious metals streamed into the market each year. We know that the expansion of an economy's scale relies on the support of even more currency. A wealthy merchant and city lord by the name of Midas devised a devious plan exploiting this very concept: What if I possessed all the world's gold? Wouldn't my city-state be unrivaled? He prayed to a certain Titan (some opine that it was Georios, some thought it was Zagreus, and others thought the patron god was Phagousa, but this remains a subject of great debate to this day), attaining the ability to control mineral resources using sinister rituals, and consolidated the entirety of Amphoreus' precious metal deposits in the mountains of his domain. He then announced this circumstance, demanding the other city-states to bend the knee, or there would be a dearth of future precious metals. Even so, history always finds a way. After precious metal was monopolized, the city-states did not cease their daily trade — Phagousa's city gathered shells, Georios' city gathered stones, Aquila's city bundled feathers... The people once again returned to the days of barter, and life went on as usual — it was only inter-city trade that was untenable. The irony was that these sundries were portable and plentiful, increasing people's enthusiasm in trade. To quell this farce, Talanton overturned the scale, turning bountiful gravel into weights enchanted with divinity, and established it as the common currency across all city-states, which are the Balance Coins of today — encompassing both the benefits and drawbacks of goods and precious metals. With the Scale of Justice being the most trustworthy, with the god's personal guarantee, inter-city trade was very quickly restored. Midas went increasingly mad when he was besieged by Castrum Kremnos, and eventually turned into a statue of pure gold.

1396730654736229465: Ever since the Phantasmoon Games were created by The Laughter, each time the Phantasmoon is full, the glorious season arrives where Supplicants beat each other bloody. Cosmic powerhouses seeking the Elation either put on spectacular shows for the masses, drowning millions in comedy and fable, or throw all dignity out the window, going at each other tooth and nail while the crowd roars with laughter from the stands. In short, whether it's the victor or the Supplicant who gains the Strength of Elation, every Phantasmoon Games throughout history has been known to pull off some pretty wild stunts. Today, I have specially selected several documented (and some suspected) traces of victors whose exploits wreaked havoc across the universe, for your amusement. Fluffy According to wild tales, the conductor of the Astral Express wasn't always fluffy, not until a certain victor of the Phantasmoon Games wished for more Fluffies to populate the universe. However, in a later interview, the conductor denied this claim. Parable of the Elation Legend has it that in Amber Era 2144, Adrian Spencer Smith won the Phantasmoon Games through unknown means. Everyone held their breath, waiting for the miracle he would create, but a minute later, nothing happened in the universe. Rumors claim he wove a parable using the divine power of the Elation, but with his disappearance, this rumor can no longer be verified. The Vitality of Words In 2146 AE, a massive textual escape occurred simultaneously across the universe. On more than ten thousand planets, written words gained life and the ability to move, fleeing from information receptacles such as books and screens. The phenomenon ceased after one minute, resulting in the loss of massive amounts of technological achievements and historical documents. In the Intelligentsia Guild's database, data related to the Eden of Blessed Insight was lost on a massive scale. It is speculated that the victorious Supplicant of this incident was either one of The Cremators or Riddlers. Mourning Segmentum In 2147 AE, multiple Space Fissures appeared across several star systems including Lafcadio, Epsilon, and Heldorin, continuously emitting "cries" into the vacuum. Any living beings within 1 light-year of their vicinity would uncontrollably weep until they were outside the range. The timing of this incident coincided with the end of the Phantasmoon Games, though Intelligentsia Guild has not confirmed any correlation between the two. On the inevitable route passing through Epsilon's Mourning Segmentum, the IPC selected a new site for Interastral Peace Entertainment's headquarters, which would later become known as Astropolis. Reincarnation In 2157 AE, a Doctor of Chaos won the Phantasmoon Games and attempted to create a universe with an afterlife to dilute the sense of emptiness that death brings to life. In Lafcadio and several surrounding star systems, "phantoms of death" from the past crowded every planet. This phenomenon lasted for several system hours, causing severe disruption. It is said that the figure of a certain Astral Express Navigator briefly appeared on Adlivun. An Anecdote Rumor has it that a high-ranking executive at the Interastral Peace Corporation once participated in the Phantasmoon Games in their youth and emerged victorious. However, like countless other realities rewritten by the power of Elation, Planarcadia's historical records contain no trace of this event. Based on timeline, age, and operational scope, massive evidence points toward Oswaldo from the Marketing Development Department, but he has never responded to these claims.

Ship Name: Starfroster
Ship Type: Can't you tell just by looking at it?
Captain: Why are you asking this?
Rebuild Date: Ah, so many questions... Who sent you?
Rebuild Location: That's it, I'm calling the cops.

Following a joint consultation with multiple expert Masked Fools and Mourning Actors, we have reached the following conclusion: Starfroster has been eaten. Every last atom. Not a scrap wasted, something worth celebrating, as it speaks highly of our culinary skills.

To prevent similar food safety issues from occurring in the future, the following changes will be implemented during reconstruction.

I. Hull Structure
Deck: The deck and superstructure were previously prone to warping under heat. The flooring has since been replaced with more durable maltose.
Mast: The previous biscuit-stick material was too brittle. During reconstruction, crushed hazelnuts were added to the chocolate mixture to set and reinforce the mast.
Gunwale: The gunwale previously posed a risk of accidental falls. During reconstruction, the edges were raised using butter cookies.
Cabin: The cabin walls previously leaked black tea. During reconstruction, they were sealed with maple syrup. The sponge cake mattress was too firm, so the egg yolk ratio has been adjusted.

II. Propulsion System
Engine: Inspection findings indicate that the chocolate bar and flip cake on the engine sustained damage during combat. The affected areas have been patched up with bean paste frosting during reconstruction.
Fuel: Crew feedback indicates that the Wishpower tank is prone to damage. Going forward, a designated crew member will need to regularly consume portions of the hull to maintain Wishpower flow and prevent rusting. (Tentative assignee: Dewide Chungus)
Propeller: The pretzel knots are absolutely delicious and relatively healthy. No changes recommended, leave as is.

III. Weapon Systems
Cannon Barrel: The main cannon's waffle cone is prone to wear and tear, so it has been replaced with a more durable cream horn during reconstruction. For budgetary reasons, the secondary cannon still uses a waffle cone.
Ammo: Standard ammunition has been restocked, including jelly beans, candy corn, and hard candies.

Overall Rating: A
Cleared for departure. Delicious and delightful.
